plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers that attract bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated in gardens and fields for essential oils, culinary use, and ornamental borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence typically peak in early to mid July, and the plant's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads composed of bright yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. The heads track the sun when young and are grown for oil, seeds, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France, and Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually made up of thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern, and each one can become a seed.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with drooping pink-purple petals around a spiky orange-brown central cone. It is a magnet for pollinators and goldfinches, and is also popular in herbal remedies.
plants.location: Native to the eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; widely cultivated in gardens
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, a reference to the prickly central cone of the flower.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub that produces the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl-shaped crown of pink-tipped bracts around a central cluster of florets. Adapted to fire-prone fynbos landscapes in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from autumn through spring (peak around July to November in some regions)
plants.location: Fynbos of South Africa's Western and Eastern Cape; South Africa's national flower
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the oldest flowering plants on Earth, dating back around 300 million years, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus for its great diversity of forms.
